chunks: We were told by my father, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Abdullah bin Ja'far al-Himyari, from Ahmad bin Muhammad bin Khalid, from Uthman bin Isa, from an old man from the people of Medina, that he said: I asked Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him,

about a man who drinks and does not stop until he is satisfied. He said: Is satisfaction but that? I said: They say that it is (like) the drinking of thirsty cattle? He said: They have lied. The drinking of thirsty cattle is only that which the Name of Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, has not been mentioned upon.

key_terms.شَرِبُ الْهِيمِ: the drinking of thirsty cattle (a specific term for drinking until full)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between ordinary drinking and 'sharib al-him' according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq records this dialogue to distinguish between the physical act of quenching thirst and the ritual state of 'sharib al-him' (drinking like a thirsty camel), which requires the invocation of Allah's name. The Imam clarifies that the specific jurisprudential implication of 'sharib al-him' applies only when the Name of Allah is not mentioned over the drink, thereby refuting the claim that mere satisfaction of thirst constitutes this state. This highlights the Shia emphasis on the spiritual dimension of daily acts, where dhikr transforms mundane actions into acts of worship.
